clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts or short selling).
why_it_matters: A collar with tenor under three months or a forward-style structure may be characterised as a short-term dealing; tenor should exceed three months.

clause: if the approval is given during or after trading on one day, the order for the dealing must be lodged or otherwise authorised before the close of trading on the second trading day after the approval is given.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar must be signed within two clear trading days and clearance can be withdrawn until the dealing is authorised, so documentation must be ready before clearance is sought.

clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Even a permissible hedge by a Permitted Restricted Person may be refused without reasons on reputational grounds, after confirmation with two Disclosure Committee members.

clause: transferring legal ownership of securities, even where beneficial ownership does not change
why_it_matters: Transferring collared shares to a bank nominee or custodian is a dealing requiring clearance, separately from the collar itself.

clause: a company or any other entity which the team member or director has an ability to control or significantly influence.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust or controlled company does not avoid the hedging or secured financing bans.

clause: Derivatives ... includes the following if they relate to or derive value from Sigma Shares ...: put or call options, exchange traded options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, depositary receipts, structured financial products, swaps, contracts for difference, spread bets, caps and collars and any other hedging or investment arrangement
why_it_matters: An OTC collar is squarely a Derivative and, through the Sigma Shares definition, a dealing in Sigma Shares requiring Chairman clearance and subject to Closed Periods and the unvested/holding-lock ban.

clause: Sigma Team Members may use derivatives in relation to Sigma Shares which have vested, provided any dealing in those derivatives complies with the other requirements of this policy and the Sigma Shares are not subject to a holding lock.
why_it_matters: There is no general hedging ban for directors or executives; the put and call legs over vested, unlocked shares are expressly contemplated.

clause: Team Members are prohibited from entering margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of Sigma Shares or in relation to which Sigma Shares may be used as security against loan repayment.
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is caught if characterised as a margin loan arrangement; the stated rationale (lender-compelled sale in a Closed Period) means a bank facility with LVR triggers or enforcement rights is likely treated the same way.

clause: Sigma Team Members who acquire Sigma Shares must not dispose of those shares, or enter arrangements (such as margin loans) which could result in those shares being disposed of, within 12 months of acquisition.
why_it_matters: A collar with physical settlement or a secured loan with enforcement rights over shares acquired within the past 12 months is a prohibited arrangement; the collar should cover only shares held (or LTI/SPP/ESP shares acquired) at least 12 months earlier or fall within the carve-outs.

clause: Sigma Team Members are prohibited from entering short selling or stock lending arrangements in relation to Sigma Shares.
why_it_matters: The bank cannot borrow the collared shares from the executive to hedge its own position or to structure the facility as a securities loan.

clause: Team Member means any full time, part time or casual employee of any member of Sigma Group and extends to any secondee, contractor or consultant of, or adviser to, any member of Sigma Group whose terms of engagement require them, or who have been given written notice ... to comply with this policy as though they were an employee.
why_it_matters: Sections 11 and 12 (12-month holding, derivatives, margin loans) are addressed to Team Members, so their application to non-executive Directors, who are Specified Persons but not employees, depends on their engagement terms.

clause: No clearance to trade will be given during a Closed Period as these are periods when the risk of insider trading, or the appearance of insider trading is high.
why_it_matters: Entry, roll, unwind and settlement of the collar must all fall in open periods; only the Chairman's extraordinary-circumstances dispensation can override this.

clause: A clearance to undertake the proposed dealing will be valid for two business days ... Timeframes beyond 2 days require the approval of the Sigma Chairman.
why_it_matters: A collar must be priced and executed within two business days of clearance unless the Chairman approves a longer window.

clause: A clearance to trade should not be granted where: there is a matter in relation to which inside information in respect of Sigma Shares (whether the Specified Person knows about the matter or not) when the Specified Person requests clearance or proposes to deal in Sigma Shares
why_it_matters: Clearance can be refused without reasons because of a matter the executive is unaware of, and refusal must be kept confidential from the bank.

clause: the blocking of off market dealings for Specified Persons where shares are held through issuer sponsored holdings without prior clearance ... monitor all trades by Specified Person via share registry trading alerts
why_it_matters: Transfer of issuer-sponsored shares to a bank custodian or nominee will be blocked at the registry without clearance and any movement will be flagged to the Company Secretary.

clause: The additional restrictions on Specified Persons in Chapter 4 do not apply to dealing by a Specified Person or their Associate that constitutes or involves, or results directly from, any of the acts or circumstances set out below.
why_it_matters: The section 17 exceptions relieve only the clearance requirement, not the Closed Period, 12-month or margin loan rules, and there is no secured-lender enforcement exception.

clause: a company, trust or other entity that A or any of their family members referred to above controls (whether alone or jointly with each other)
why_it_matters: A collar or loan entered through a family trust or controlled company is treated as the Specified Person's own dealing and needs clearance.

clause: Personnel are not permitted at any time to: ... enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of the Company's securities;
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is an 'other secured financing arrangement' expressly prohibited for all personnel at any time, regardless of vesting state, with no approval or exemption route.

clause: Deal ... Includes, in relation to securities: Any acquisition or disposal, or agreement to acquire or dispose: Entering into a contract with the purpose to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations
why_it_matters: A put/call collar is squarely a contract to avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations, so entry, unwind, roll and settlement are each dealings requiring clearance and a trading window for Directors, Senior Executives and designated employees.

clause: enter into transactions with securities (or any derivative thereof) which limit the economic risk of any unvested entitlements awarded under an equity-based remuneration scheme, or otherwise awarded, or which will be offered by the Company in the future (eg hedging).
why_it_matters: The ban reaches entitlements 'otherwise awarded' and future offers, so the collar must be sized strictly to vested shares and a bank should confirm that no part of the hedged parcel is referable to unvested or prospective awards.

clause: Clearance may be given for such a person to sell (but not purchase) Evolution securities in a prohibited trading period.
why_it_matters: Closed-period relief cannot cover entry into a collar or a purchase to close a written call; only an outright sale in severe financial difficulty or under a court order can be cleared, and only by the Executive Chairman.

clause: The trading windows for Directors, Senior Executives and designated employees are: (a) For a period of thirty days after the release of the Company's half yearly results; ... (g) For a period of fifteen days following the release of the Company's quarterly reports.
why_it_matters: The policy uses narrow open windows (15 or 30 days after specified releases) rather than closed periods, so the collar must be documented and executed within one of those windows and within five business days of clearance.

clause: The Company reserves the right to impose a restriction on trading during any period, including one that would otherwise fall within a permitted trading window.
why_it_matters: A trading window can be closed without notice, which may block a scheduled unwind, roll or physical settlement of the collar.

clause: A clearance to deal can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances. The Company's decision to refuse clearance is final and binding on the person seeking clearance.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar can become unexecutable between clearance and pricing, so the bank should price and sign promptly within the five-business-day validity.

clause: Directors and Senior Executives (or any family member or associate over whom they have influence) have additional dealing restrictions
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or the secured loan through a family member, trust or controlled entity does not escape the window, clearance or secured-financing rules.

clause: engage in short-term trading (less than one month), or short selling of the Company's securities at any time;
why_it_matters: A collar or any related share purchase/sale that is opened and closed within one month risks characterisation as short-term trading; tenor should exceed one month.

clause: Remedial action may include a requirement that the person who sold Evolution securities in breach of the Policy to donate any profits earned to charity.
why_it_matters: Any profit from a non-compliant collar or forced sale could be required to be disgorged to charity, in addition to disciplinary action.

topic: secured financing is consent-based, not banned
clause: You and your Associates are not permitted to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Amcor Securities without the prior consent of the Company Secretary.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is available to Directors, Executive Team Members and co-workers on a single consent from the Company Secretary, making Amcor one of the policies under which the structure is achievable.

clause: If you are an Executive Team Member, you are prohibited from Trading in a Blackout Period in Derivatives, financial products issued or created over or in respect of Amcor Securities. Examples of these financial products include swaps, caps and collars.
why_it_matters: Collars are named and are prohibited only during Blackout Periods, which confirms by implication that a collar entered outside a Blackout Period with the required notification is contemplated by the policy.

clause: The Amcor Share Trading Policy does not apply to ... an involuntary disposal of Amcor Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights.
why_it_matters: A bank enforcing its security or a margin call sale during a Blackout Period falls outside the policy entirely, so the lender's enforcement rights do not put the executive in breach - a materially better position than policies that treat forced sales as a breach.

clause: Short-term Trading refers to Trading in and out of Securities within a consecutive three month period.
why_it_matters: Because Securities include Derivatives, the collar's tenor and any unwind, roll, restrike or early termination must be more than three months apart, ruling out short-dated or frequently rolled structures.

clause: The notification must confirm the Executive Team Member will be in compliance with the minimum shareholding policy after the trade, (if applicable).
why_it_matters: The confirmer must be satisfied the Executive Team Member still meets the minimum shareholding after the collar, so the collared parcel must be sized to leave the minimum holding unhedged unless the Minimum Shareholding Policy says otherwise.

topic: two week trading window in the notification
clause: specify the proposed dates of the trade which should be no more than two weeks
why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of the collar and the secured loan must all be completed inside the two-week window nominated in the notification, or a fresh notification and confirmation is needed.

clause: A clearance to trade can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances; ... A decision to refuse clearance is final and binding ... the person seeking the clearance must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
why_it_matters: The bank cannot be told why a trade was blocked and confirmation can be withdrawn between pricing and settlement, so the trade documentation needs a condition precedent for subsisting clearance at execution.

clause: IF YOU DO COME INTO POSSESSION OF INSIDE INFORMATION AFTER RECEIVING A CLEARANCE TO TRADE, YOU MUST NOT TRADE DESPITE HAVING RECEIVED THE CLEARANCE.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar can become unexecutable at any point before signing, so the bank should expect a walk-away right on the executive's side.

clause: A person is an “Associate” if a Director or co-worker is acting in concert with that person or if a Director or co-worker has, or can be regarded as having, investment control or influence over that person. Examples ... a trust of which the Director or co-worker ... are the trustee or beneficiary; ... a company which the Director or co-worker or their family controls.
why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a family trust or controlled company does not avoid the consent, notification and Blackout Period requirements.

clause: Following the end of each financial year, all Directors and Executive Team Members must certify to the Company Secretary that they and their Associates are in compliance with this policy (or advise of any breaches of this policy).
why_it_matters: An outstanding collar and secured loan must remain compliant for its whole life and is re-attested annually, so a structure that drifts out of the minimum shareholding or is rolled inside three months surfaces at certification.

clause: “Derivatives” includes warrants, exchange traded and over the counter options and contracts for differences.
why_it_matters: There is no venue limitation, so an OTC put and call written with a bank is inside the derivatives regime rather than outside an exchange-limited ban.

clause: any other period that the Board specifies from time to time. If the Board specifies any other period, communications will be sent to you.
why_it_matters: Additional blackouts are notified rather than kept confidential, so an executive can tell the bank a window is closed without breaching confidentiality, though the reason may not be disclosable.

topic: any form of security is banned
clause: Designated Persons must not enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over Santos securities.
why_it_matters: This is broader than a margin lending ban and kills the funded leg outright: a loan secured on the collared shares, and any charge, pledge or security trust over them, is prohibited for every Designated Person with no consent route.

clause: Short-term or speculative dealing includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, forward contracts and short selling.
why_it_matters: Naming forward contracts as speculative dealing blocks prepaid forward and forward sale alternatives to a collar, and invites the same characterisation of a tightly struck zero-cost collar that is economically a forward sale.

topic: no waiver over the financing and hedging bans
clause: A written application to deal with Santos securities outside a Trading Window due to severe financial difficulty or other exceptional circumstances may be made to the Company Secretary.
why_it_matters: The only discretionary relief in the policy is from the Trading Window restriction, so the sections 4.8, 4.9 and 5 prohibitions cannot be waived even in hardship.

clause: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances, could the proposed dealing be perceived to be inappropriate for someone in my position? ... Clearance to deal under this Policy will not be granted where the person providing clearance does not consider that the ‘front page test’ is satisfied.
why_it_matters: Even an unfunded collar over vested unrestricted shares can be refused on perception grounds alone, with no reasons given and no appeal, so the bank cannot rely on the technical permissibility of the derivative legs.

clause: Designated Persons may not assume that a Trading Window is open, even after the relevant ASX announcement or Annual General Meeting. ... A Trading Window may be varied, suspended or withdrawn by the Board or the CEO at any time.
why_it_matters: Execution windows are discretionary and can be withdrawn mid-window, so any collar entry, roll or unwind must be documented as conditional on a subsisting open window at the moment of dealing.

clause: Any clearance given under section 4.3 or 4.6 will be provided in writing and lasts for 5 business days or such other period specified in the notice of clearance. ... Any clearance may be revoked or withdrawn or the clearance period shortened or lengthened and may include conditions at the company's absolute discretion.
why_it_matters: Pricing and execution of the derivative legs must complete within 5 business days and can be conditioned or revoked at any point before dealing, and a refusal must be kept confidential from the bank.

clause: In the case of an on-market trade, the dealing occurs at execution (but not settlement) of the trade. In the case of an off-market trade, the dealing occurs at settlement of the trade.
why_it_matters: For an OTC collar the dealing is timed at settlement rather than trade date, so physical settlement or delivery must itself fall inside an open window with subsisting clearance, not merely the trade date.

clause: “securities” include ... financial products relating to a company's securities (for example, warrants and other derivative products), irrespective of whether the financial products are created by the company or by third parties.
why_it_matters: A bank-written OTC put and call are securities in their own right, so the Trading Window, clearance, short-term dealing and front page test rules all attach to the option legs, not just to the shares.

clause: Designated Persons must ... ensure that their Connected Persons do not engage in any short-term or speculative dealing or margin lending arrangements.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or the secured loan through a spouse, family trust or controlled company does not escape the section 4.9 ban.

clause: margin lending and other such arrangements could result in a forced sale of securities in breach of insider trading laws or this policy, such as during a period when you are in possession of or could be perceived to be in possession of inside information.
why_it_matters: Santos treats lender enforcement as capable of breaching the policy rather than excluding it, so even for non-Designated employees a secured structure carries policy risk on enforcement.

clause: No Hedging or Pledging. Covered Persons are prohibited from hedging or pledging any equity compensation or Company securities that they hold directly.
why_it_matters: This single sentence kills both legs of a funded collar at once: the put and call are a hedge and the loan security is a pledge, for every Covered Person and their family members and controlled entities, with no vesting, tier or size qualifier and no clearance route.

clause: prohibited from hedging or pledging any equity compensation or Company securities that they hold directly
why_it_matters: The only textual soft spot in the ban is the words 'hold directly', but the Scope section makes family members and controlled entities Covered Persons in their own right, so an indirect holding structure does not create a workable exemption and any attempt would need General Counsel confirmation.

clause: This prohibition includes, but is not limited to, trading in Company-based put or call option contracts, trading in straddles and the like.
why_it_matters: An OTC bilateral put and call with a bank is caught exactly as a listed option would be, and a two-leg collar is closer to a 'straddle and the like' than a plain option, so there is no exchange/OTC arbitrage.

clause: all of the Company's securities, including ... CHESS Depositary Interests representing the Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock and derivative securities (including stock options, put or call options and other similar securities)
why_it_matters: A collar written over ASX-quoted CDIs rather than Nasdaq-listed common stock is inside the Policy, so the ASX line offers no separate route.

clause: For the avoidance of doubt, transactions pursuant to Rule 10b5-1 Trading Plans that are effected in accordance with this Policy may occur notwithstanding the other prohibitions included herein.
why_it_matters: This is the widest permission in the document and could in principle cover disposals inside a black-out, but Appendix A clause 4 expressly forbids any corresponding or hedging position over the plan securities, so a 10b5-1 plan is an alternative to a collar, not a wrapper for one.

clause: This Policy may be modified or an exception granted with approval of the Company's Board of Directors or the Company's General Counsel, where the circumstances make such modification or exception appropriate, in compliance with applicable law.
why_it_matters: The only conceivable path to a funded collar is a bespoke Board or General Counsel exception, which would sit against a proxy-disclosed anti-hedging commitment and would still have to survive Section 16, Rule 144 and short-swing profit analysis.

clause: A short sale is a sale of securities not owned by the seller or, if owned, not delivered against such sale within twenty (20) days thereafter (a 'short against the box').
why_it_matters: Any physically settled forward or delayed-delivery leg where shares are not delivered within twenty days is a prohibited short sale, which forecloses prepaid variable forward structures as well as collars.

clause: Additional black-out periods may be implemented from time to time ... Any person made aware of any such additional black-out period shall not disclose the existence of the black-out to anyone else inside or outside the Company.
why_it_matters: Undisclosed event-driven black-outs can freeze entry, roll, unwind or settlement at any time and cannot be flagged to a counterparty bank, so any structure would need documentation permitting silent suspension.

clause: the transaction must be executed within five Trading Days after the approval is obtained, but regardless may not be executed if the Restricted Person acquires material, non-public information concerning the Company or its securities during that time.
why_it_matters: Even for permitted transactions the pricing window is five Trading Days and clearance falls away automatically on receipt of inside information, so a bank must accept a short, revocable execution window.

clause: Any Company securities purchased on the open market by a Restricted Person must be held for a minimum of six (6) months.
why_it_matters: Combined with Section 16 short-swing profit disgorgement, this rules out any collar tenor or early unwind that could put a disposal within six months of an open-market purchase by a director or Section 16 officer.

clause: The prohibition against trading during the Black-Out Period also prohibits the fulfillment of 'limit orders' by any broker for Restricted Persons, and the brokers with whom any such 'limit order' is placed must be informed of such prohibition at the time such 'limit order' is placed.
why_it_matters: Automatic third-party execution is treated as the executive's own trading, so a lender's or counterparty's price-triggered sale or delivery during a black-out would be a Policy breach attributed to the executive.

clause: transferring shares to an entity that does not involve a change in the beneficial ownership of the shares (for example, transferring shares from one brokerage account to another brokerage account that a Covered Person controls)
why_it_matters: Moving shares into a collateral or custody account is not itself a 'transaction' needing clearance, but the security interest granted over them is still a prohibited pledge, so the transfer carve-out gives no help.

clause: After termination of employment or other service, any Covered Person who is aware of material, non-public information regarding the Company or its securities is prohibited from trading in Company securities until that information has become public or is no longer material.
why_it_matters: A departing executive cannot assume that leaving releases the restrictions in time to unwind or settle a structure.
