Designated Persons must not trade in Brambles Derivatives.
why_it_matters: A bank-written put and call is an 'option granted by a third party' and a 'collar', so the derivative legs of a funded collar are prohibited by name for all Designated Persons regardless of vesting state.

clause: A Designated Person must not grant a Security Interest over any Brambles Securities they hold. ... Security Interest means a pledge, lien, charge, mortgage or other encumbrance.
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is prohibited outright; the ban is not limited to margin loans and has no approval route.

clause: If a Designated Person were to take out a margin loan and the security for that loan included Brambles Securities, the lender may be able to sell or otherwise Deal in those Securities. This would be so notwithstanding that, at the relevant time, there may be a Closed Period or the Designated Person may be in possession of price sensitive information ... This could cause the Designated Person to be in breach of this Policy.
why_it_matters: The policy treats a lender's enforcement sale as the Designated Person's own breach, so lender enforcement rights cannot be relied on even if a security interest were somehow permitted.

clause: Designated Persons may still acquire Brambles Securities through a margin or other investment loan if Brambles Securities are not used as security for that loan.
why_it_matters: Only a loan with no security over Brambles Securities is open, which removes the secured-loan element that defines a funded collar.

clause: their nominee, including an investment manager managing funds on their behalf; a trust of which they, any member of their family, or any family controlled company, are the trustee or beneficiary; ... a company which they or their family control.
why_it_matters: Routing a collar or secured loan through a family trust, nominee or controlled company remains within the derivatives and Security Interest bans.

clause: Approval can be given or refused at Brambles' discretion without giving reasons. A refusal to approve a request to Deal in Brambles Securities is final and binding ... The Designated Person will be notified if the clearance position changes within those two business days.
why_it_matters: Any permitted Dealing must be executed within two business days and clearance can be withdrawn before execution, which matters for pricing and settlement of any structured transaction.

clause: The names and addresses of Designated Persons will be supplied to Brambles' share registry from time to time, for the purpose of investigating compliance with this Policy and with the insider trading prohibition.
why_it_matters: Any transfer of collared shares to a bank nominee or custodian is likely to be detected through registry monitoring.

clause: Amended: ... and 3 July 2017
why_it_matters: The lodged policy is dated July 2017 and may have been superseded; the bank should confirm the current version before relying on it.

topic: absolute hedging ban for senior people
clause: A Designated Person or one of his or her Associates must not engage in Dealings undertaken for Short Swing Profit or Hedging Transactions at any time.
why_it_matters: The put and call legs of a collar are squarely a Hedging Transaction, so no director, CEO, CFO, Financial Controller or Vice President (or their family, family company or trust) can enter a collar at all, whether the shares are vested or not and whether the window is open or closed.

topic: hedging definition is economic, not instrument-based
clause: Hedging Transaction means Dealing in call or put options involving Company Securities or in other derivative Company Securities that provide a means to limit the economic risk of Company Securities.
why_it_matters: It names call and put options directly and then sweeps in any other derivative that limits economic risk, so a bank cannot restructure the collar as a swap, prepaid forward or CFD to avoid it.

topic: exemption authority reaches the hedging ban
clause: An employee of the James Hardie Group may request a specific exemption from the prohibitions in Section 2 ... An exemption may be approved by the CFO or General Counsel, or in the case of an exemption for a Director or direct report to the CEO, by the Chairman of the Board or Audit Committee.
why_it_matters: This is the only route to a collar for a Designated Person: the hedging ban sits in Section 2 and is therefore waivable, but only on hardship-style 'good reasons', only if it does not undermine the spirit of the Policy, and the waiver is reported to the Board.

topic: hedging permitted for non-designated staff on notification only
clause: An Insider or one of his or her Associates (other than a Designated Person) wishing to Deal in Company Securities through a Hedging Transaction of vested shares ... may only do so if such Dealing is within the Open Period and the Insider or his or her Associate notifies the Compliance Officer of such Dealing within 7 days after such Dealing.
why_it_matters: Below Designated Person level a collar over vested shares is available with no pre-approval at all, provided it is struck inside the four-week Open Period and reported within 7 days.

clause: Deal means buying, selling or otherwise trading in, and gifting, pledging, accepting or exercising Securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg is not prohibited, but the security granted over the collared shares is itself a Dealing, so it must be struck in an Open Period and, for Designated Persons, pre-cleared in writing five ASX trading days in advance.

topic: no secured financing or margin lending ban
clause: The Policy contains no reference to margin loans, margin calls, secured financing arrangements, forced sales by a lender, or price triggers.
why_it_matters: Unusually for an ASX policy the funding leg is unrestricted in substance, so the obstacle to a funded collar here is entirely the hedge legs, not the loan.

topic: short window and long lead time
clause: Open Period means the period of four weeks following a quarterly profit announcement ... (such four-week period not beginning until two Australian Securities Exchange trading days after the announcement has been released to the market) ... not less than five Australian Securities Exchange trading days before the date of that intended Dealing.
why_it_matters: Even where a structure is permitted, the five-trading-day notice consumes a quarter of the four-week window, so pricing must be agreed well before the window opens and the trade re-priced on execution.

clause: If the Compliance Officer approves the intended Dealing, such Dealing must take place within the Open Period following the approval (or such other period specified by the Compliance Officer).
why_it_matters: A cleared pledge or unwind must settle before the Open Period closes, so a collar's roll, restrike or termination has to be scheduled against the quarterly calendar rather than a market date.

clause: Short Swing Profit means any profit realised or expected to be realised by any Designated Person or any of his or her Associates from any purchase and sale, or any sale and purchase, of Company Securities within any period of less than six months.
why_it_matters: Because Securities include derivatives, even an exempted collar for a Designated Person could not be unwound, rolled or physically settled within six months of the opening legs.

clause: Associate means ... a family company of the Insider (i.e., a company in which an Insider, his or her domestic partner, a relative or family trust is a director, shareholder or adviser); or any trust or estate in which an Insider is a trustee, beneficiary or a director of a trustee or an adviser.
why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a family company, family trust or an estate does not escape the Designated Person hedging ban, and the Insider must actively inform those persons of their obligations.

clause: The Compliance Officer may prohibit some or all Insiders and their Associates from Dealing in specific Securities ... The Compliance Officer may further prohibit one or more groups of Insiders and Associates from Dealing in Securities during certain periods, including Open Periods.
why_it_matters: An Open Period is not a guaranteed execution window: the Compliance Officer can close it for a group at any time, which must be treated as a condition precedent to pricing rather than a settled fact.

clause: terminating or suspending an Insider's employment contract, and, if applicable, any such termination shall constitute a termination 'for cause' under such contract; or declaring the Insider ineligible for future participation in the James Hardie Group's equity incentive plans.
why_it_matters: A collar entered by a Designated Person without an exemption is a for-cause termination event and forfeits future equity, so the bank should require written evidence of clearance or exemption before trading.

topic: restricted dealings bind only KMP and Lead Team
clause: KMP and South32 Lead Team members must not undertake any of the following dealings ... (a) trade in derivative products ... (d) enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements ... (e) enter into any hedging arrangements that limit his or her exposure to the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: The derivatives, hedging and secured financing bans are confined to KMP, South32 Lead Team members and their PCAs; a senior executive below the Lead Team faces only Insider Trading rules (and pre-approval plus closed periods if designated a Restricted Employee), so a funded collar is arguable for that population but not for the target directors and executives.

topic: hedging ban is not limited to unvested shares
clause: enter into any hedging arrangements that limit his or her exposure to the Company's securities
why_it_matters: Unlike policies that only ban hedging of unvested incentive securities, this prohibition covers a KMP's entire holding, so vesting the shares first does not open a route to a collar.

clause: Dealing includes a wide range of transactions such as using the Company's shares as security for a loan and entering into any derivative contract which relates to the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: Both the loan leg and the option legs of a funded collar are dealings, so each requires prior approval, falls inside the closed periods, and triggers same-day notification to Company Secretariat and disclosure to ASX, LSE, JSE and the FCA.

clause: If, however, a member of the KMP South32 Lead Team or a Restricted Employee needs to deal (to sell but not buy) in securities during a closed period due to exceptional circumstances
why_it_matters: Even in hardship there is no route to enter, roll or unwind a collar during a closed period, because buying (including buying a put or closing out a written call) is excluded; only an outright sale can be approved.

clause: the relevant approver may determine that this Policy does not apply to other types of dealings in respect of the Company's securities (for example: those listed in section 6.1 of ASX Listing Rules Guidance Note 27), provided that no such determination would breach any relevant law or regulation.
why_it_matters: This is the only conceivable route to a bank collar for a KMP, but it sits in the 'dealings excluded from this Policy' section rather than in section 6.9 and is illustrated only by routine GN27 exclusions, so it should not be relied on without a board-level waiver.

clause: The approved dealing must occur within two business days following approval (or such other time specified in the approval), otherwise the approval is no longer effective and approval must be sought again.
why_it_matters: Any approved transaction must be priced and executed within two business days, which is tight for negotiating and documenting an OTC collar and loan, although the approver can specify a longer window.

clause: company, a legal person, trust partnership or other entity, the managerial responsibilities of which are discharged by the KMP ... which is directly or indirectly controlled by such a person or is set up for the benefit of such a person, or the economic interests of which are substantially equivalent to those of such a person.
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or the borrowing through an SPV, family trust or spouse does not escape the prohibitions, and KMP must file a list of these persons with the Company.

clause: any other period that is specified as a closed period for dealings from time to time. In particular, this could include a period specified as a closed period if required to do so by applicable law.
why_it_matters: Additional closed periods can be declared without notice and the Policy does not say they will be announced, so execution risk sits with the executive on any dated collar entry or unwind.

clause: where securities in the Company granted under an employee, executive or director equity plan cease to be held under the terms of that plan, any dealings in those securities must only occur in accordance with this Policy.
why_it_matters: Vested shares released from the incentive plan fall squarely back under the Policy, including the section 6.9 hedging and secured financing bans, so there is no post-vesting freedom to collar them.

clause: Breaches of this Policy may also lead to disciplinary action being taken against the Employee, including forfeiture of securities and/or suspension or termination of employment.
why_it_matters: Forfeiture of securities is an express sanction, which for a bank would put the collateral itself at risk if the structure were found to breach the Policy.

clause: Derivatives has the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act and includes options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, swaps, caps and collars.
why_it_matters: The instrument the bank proposes is named in the Policy's own definitions, so there is no ambiguity that a collar is within scope and, over fully vested unrestricted Securities, within what D.5 permits.

clause: once any applicable Computershare Securities have vested, such that any Computershare imposed time and performance hurdles have been satisfied (and any disposal restrictions on vested Securities have been lifted), Derivatives may be used in relation to those Securities
why_it_matters: This is an express permission, not merely silence, so a collar over fully vested and unrestricted shares is contemplated by the Policy; the bank should obtain confirmation from the Company Secretary that all plan disposal restrictions on the specific parcel have lapsed.

topic: secured lending permitted with a distress-only notice
clause: A Designated Person must inform the relevant Nominated Director immediately if all of the following circumstances apply: the Designated Person holds Computershare Securities that have been provided as security in relation to a lending arrangement; circumstances have arisen in which the secured lender demands payment ...; and there is a risk that the demand will not be able to be satisfied without the disposal of Computershare Securities.
why_it_matters: There is no prohibition on the loan leg and no inception or annual disclosure, but the executive must give the Nominated Director immediate notice once the bank demands payment in circumstances where shares may have to be sold, and the facility documents should oblige the bank to alert the borrower in time for that notice.

topic: forced sale is an exempt dealing
clause: an involuntary disposal of Computershare Securities that results from a lender exercising its rights under a secured lending arrangement provided that the Designated Person had, before the disposal, informed the Nominated Director of the risk of the disposal in accordance with Section D.11
why_it_matters: Unusually favourable for a funded structure: lender enforcement, including during a Prohibited Period, is carved out of the Section D requirements entirely, but the carve-out is conditional on the D.11 notice having been given first, so a sudden enforcement without notice would put the executive in breach.

topic: clearance required even in an open window for derivatives
clause: Subject to Section D.5 of this Policy, if a Designated Person intends to Deal in a Derivative over Computershare Securities during a Dealing Window then the Designated Person must obtain clearance to Deal in accordance with the procedure set out in Section D.4.
why_it_matters: Ordinary share trades in a Dealing Window need no clearance, but every derivative leg does, so entry, roll, restrike, partial unwind and physical settlement of the collar each require a separate written clearance.

topic: no fixed clearance validity, deal as soon as possible
clause: A Designated Person who receives clearance to Deal from the Nominated Director in accordance with this procedure must Deal as soon as possible after receiving the Nominated Director's response
why_it_matters: There is no stated number of days for which a clearance remains valid, but the obligation to deal 'as soon as possible' means the collar should be pre-negotiated and priced so it can be executed immediately on clearance.

clause: If clearance to Deal is granted that clearance is not an approval of the proposed Dealing. Each Designated Person remains personally responsible for any decision to Deal and for their compliance with the insider trading laws and this Policy.
why_it_matters: Clearance gives the bank no comfort that the company has blessed the structure, so the bank cannot rely on it as a representation of policy compliance and should take its own compliance representations from the executive.

clause: Dealing Window means: the four week period from ... the ASX trading day after the date on which Computershare's half-year financial results are released ... full-year financial results are released ... the annual general meeting is held
why_it_matters: This is an open-window policy: for most of the year a Designated Person is outside both a Dealing Window and a Prohibited Period and needs specific clearance under D.3, so scheduling collar entry and any unwind inside one of the three four-week windows is the low-friction path.

clause: and any other period that may be designated as a prohibited period by the Board from time to time and notified to each Designated Person.
why_it_matters: An ad hoc Prohibited Period can block collar entry or a voluntary unwind at short notice, though it must be notified to the Designated Person, so the executive will know.

clause: A Designated Person must not enter into an arrangement to short sell Computershare Securities at any time.
why_it_matters: The collar must be fully covered by shares the executive actually holds; an overhedge, or a cash-settled structure over notional shares in excess of the holding, would breach D.10 even inside a Dealing Window.

clause: Connected Person means, in relation to a Designated Person: (a) the Designated Person's partner and dependants ...; (b) a company or other entity of which the Designated Person is a director; (c) a trustee where the beneficiaries of the trust include the Designated Person; and (d) any other entity which the Designated Person has an ability to control.
why_it_matters: A collar written by a family trust or controlled company is treated as within the Policy, so the same clearance and notification path applies wherever the collateral shares are held.

clause: In accordance with ASX Listing Rule 3.19A, the Company Secretary will lodge with the ASX the necessary notification of the change in the Director's interest in Computershare Securities within five business days after the Dealing is transacted.
why_it_matters: A Director's collar is a Deal in Securities, so it becomes publicly disclosed via Appendix 3Y within five business days, and the bank should expect the structure to be visible to the market.

clause: The additional dealing restrictions set out above do not apply to ... a disposal of securities of FPHC that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement. However, such dealings are still subject to the prohibitions against insider trading.
why_it_matters: A bank enforcing security over collared shares (even in a black-out) does not breach the policy, though the executive remains exposed to insider trading law if enforcement is discretionary while they hold material information.

clause: The policy contains no prohibition on margin lending, secured financing, hedging, short selling or short-term trading; the only rules are insider trading, black-outs and consent for Restricted Persons.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the shares, is not a 'dealing' and requires no consent; only the derivative legs are regulated.

clause: the term "securities" also extends to financial products issued or created over or in respect of securities issued by FPHC (for example, warrants and other derivative products), whether or not the financial products are created by FPHC or by third parties.
why_it_matters: A bank-written OTC put and call is a Restricted Security, so entering, unwinding or physically settling the collar requires Approver consent outside black-outs.

clause: Request for Consent form: '6. To be Transacted: On NZSX / Off Market Trade / Other Specify'; '3. Type of Transaction: Buy / Sell / Transfer'.
why_it_matters: The consent form expressly accommodates off-market and 'other' transactions, so an OTC collar can be described and cleared through the standard process.

clause: A consent is only valid for a period of 15 trading days after notification. A consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of material information prior to dealing.
why_it_matters: The collar must be priced and executed within 15 trading days of consent and becomes unexecutable if material information arises before signing.

clause: where securities in FPHC granted under an employee, executive or director equity plan cease to be held under the terms of that plan, any dealings in those securities must only occur in accordance with the Securities Dealing Policy and Guidelines and the additional dealing restrictions set out above.
why_it_matters: Vested shares released from a plan are ordinary Restricted Securities; unvested plan securities are not separately addressed, so a collar over them is not policy-prohibited but plan terms should be checked.

clause: Restricted Persons will be considered responsible for the actions of trusts and companies controlled by them. In this respect, 'control' is not to be construed in a technical way but by looking at how decisions are made in practice.
why_it_matters: A collar entered through a family trust or company controlled in practice by the executive is treated as the executive's own dealing.

clause: Securities Dealing Policy and Guidelines (2013 final), dated 27 August 2013.
why_it_matters: The policy pre-dates current ASX Guidance Note 27 expectations on hedging and margin lending, so the company may have adopted a later version; confirm currency before relying on the absence of restrictions.

clause: A sale of your Origin Securities by a third party outside your control (such as a margin lender) in a Closed Period or when you are otherwise prohibited by this Policy is a serious breach of this Policy and may result in dismissal.
why_it_matters: Even if a secured facility existed, the bank's enforcement or physical settlement of the collar during a Closed Period would put the executive in serious breach, so the structure cannot rely on lender enforcement rights.

clause: From the date of this Policy, you must not ... enter into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of Origin Securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is expressly prohibited for all personnel and Associates regardless of vesting state, with no approval route; the wording is prospective only and is silent on unwinding pre-existing arrangements.

clause: Dealing in Origin Securities during a Closed Period or Additional Prohibitions will not be permitted.
why_it_matters: No hardship or exceptional-circumstances exemption exists, so collar entry, unwind, roll or settlement must fall entirely within open windows.

clause: If you come to possess Inside Information after receiving clearance to Deal, you must not complete the trade.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar must be priced and executed within the 2-business-day validity and can become unexecutable if inside information arises before signing.

clause: If you hold Origin Securities, you must recognise that a prohibition may apply at the time you wish to sell them, and Origin will have no responsibility to you.
why_it_matters: Undisclosed Additional Prohibitions can block delivery or unwind of shares under the collar at any time, and the executive bears that risk.

clause: You must not ... enter into arrangements which result in short-term Dealing (such as margin loans) to minimise the perception of speculative trading.
why_it_matters: A short-dated collar or one with early-termination triggers may be characterised as an arrangement resulting in short-term Dealing, so tenor should exceed three months.

clause: This Policy also extends to Associates of Origin Personnel. ... a company, partnership or trust over which: (i) you have control or significant influence
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust or controlled company does not escape the secured financing ban or clearance requirement.

clause: Securities: ... any financial product; derivatives ... Dealing: ... create a derivative over Securities
why_it_matters: There is no venue limitation, so an OTC put and call with a bank is squarely a Dealing subject to clearance and windows.

clause: Directors, Employees and Contractors are prohibited from entering into a hedging transaction that is designed to limit the economic risk of holdings in Suncorp Securities, including unvested performance rights.
why_it_matters: The ban is drafted around 'holdings in Suncorp Securities' generally rather than plan or unvested securities, so a put and call collar over vested unrestricted shares is prohibited outright, and 'including unvested performance rights' reads as an extension of that scope rather than a limit on it.

topic: no waiver for the hedging ban
clause: Policy Exemptions: No exemptions apply to this Policy. The Section 8 waiver enables Prescribed Persons 'to Deal in Suncorp Securities during Closed Periods' in Exceptional Circumstances.
why_it_matters: The waiver power is confined to lifting Closed Period restrictions, so there is no mechanism by which the Chairman, Group CEO or Board could authorise a collar despite section 5.1.

clause: The Suncorp Chairman, or the Group CEO, will review any request for waiver or clearance to Deal by Prescribed Persons or their Connected Persons which involves entering into a new or increased Margin Loan or other use of Suncorp Securities as collateral in a financial transaction.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is permitted in principle subject to individual approval by the Chairman or Group CEO who may attach conditions, so the financing is not the obstacle here; the hedging ban on the derivative legs is.

topic: forced sale is an exempt dealing
clause: involuntary disposal under a margin loan: a disposal of Suncorp Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: Unusually favourable for a lender: enforcement or margin-call sale by the bank is expressly exempt from Closed Period restrictions and from the clearance requirement, so the bank's security can be realised at any time without putting the executive in breach.

topic: granting security is itself a dealing
clause: Examples of Dealing in Securities include: ... granting a mortgage, lien, charge or other security interest (such as a Margin Loan) over Securities;
why_it_matters: Executing the security document over the collared shares is a Dealing in its own right, so it needs prior written clearance, must be outside Closed Periods and must be completed inside the clearance window.

clause: Security or Securities: ... derivative products (including but not limited to warrants, exchange-traded options, over-the-counter options and contracts for differences) relating to those securities, whether or not the securities or the derivative products are issued or created by Suncorp or by third parties.
why_it_matters: The put and the call written by a bank are themselves Suncorp Securities, so every leg, roll, amendment and settlement is a separate Dealing subject to clearance and Closed Periods even before section 5.1 is considered.

clause: Short-Term Dealing ... means buying and selling the same Security within a six month period and entering into any other short term Dealings (for example, forward contracts) in relation to Securities.
why_it_matters: Even if the hedging ban did not apply, a forward-settled or short-dated collar is the express example of prohibited short-term Dealing, so any structure would need a tenor comfortably beyond six months and no early unwind.

clause: Any clearance request to Deal can be given, refused or withdrawn by Suncorp in its discretion, without giving any reasons. A decision to refuse clearance is final and binding on the person seeking clearance. If clearance to Deal is refused, the person seeking clearance must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
why_it_matters: Clearance can be withdrawn after it is given and before execution, and the executive cannot tell the bank why a trade cannot proceed, so pricing and mandate documentation must tolerate silent withdrawal.

clause: In certain circumstances the Company Secretary may be asked to restrict individuals from Dealing in Suncorp Securities who may be in possession of Price Sensitive Information for a period of time ('Restricted List').
why_it_matters: An individual can be blocked from dealing at any time outside the scheduled Closed Periods, which would prevent entry, roll, unwind or physical settlement of any structure without notice to the counterparty.

clause: A Connected Person of a Prescribed Person includes ... a company, trust or entity that the Prescribed Person (or any of their family members falling within any of the above categories) controls or has an interest in.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or the loan through a family trust, SMSF or controlled company does not escape either the hedging ban or the clearance and Closed Period regime, and the 'has an interest in' limb is wider than control.

topic: hedging ban has the widest personal scope
clause: 5.1 Directors, Employees and Contractors are prohibited from entering into a hedging transaction ...
why_it_matters: The hedging ban is addressed to all Directors, Employees and Contractors rather than only to Prescribed Persons, so it catches executives well below KMP level who are otherwise free of Closed Periods and clearance.

clause: The above restriction includes all arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements but does not extend to other types of loan arrangements which may be secured by a security interest granted in respect of Scentre Group Securities. However, if a Restricted Person proposes to enter into any such security arrangement they should obtain the prior approval of the Company Secretary prior to entering into any such arrangement.
why_it_matters: This is the clause that makes a funded collar feasible: a bank term loan secured on the collared securities is expressly outside the margin lending ban and needs only the Company Secretary's prior approval, so the financing leg has a defined, single-approver route.

clause: A Restricted Person should also consult with the Company Secretary if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement is properly classified as a margin lending or security arrangement.
why_it_matters: The Company Secretary decides whether the facility is 'properly described as' margin lending, so the loan should be documented with no LVR-based margin call or top-up mechanics and the characterisation confirmed in writing before signing.

clause: a disposal of Scentre Group Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights. For the avoidance of doubt, in relation to Key Management Personnel, this does not extend to the exercise by a lender of rights under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: Enforcement or physical settlement by the bank under a non-margin secured facility is excluded from the blackout and trading restrictions even for directors and KMP, so the bank's security can be realised in a blackout period without putting the executive in breach; the carve-back bites only on margin lending, which is prohibited anyway.

topic: hedging ban is bounded to plan securities
clause: Prohibitions also apply to executives participating in the equity-linked incentive plans from entering into hedging arrangements in respect of unvested awards or awards that have vested but are held in a holding lock or otherwise the subject of deferral of delivery.
why_it_matters: There is no hedging prohibition on vested, released or ordinarily acquired securities, so a collar over unrestricted shares is not barred by this policy, but shares still in a holding lock or subject to deferred delivery must be excluded from the collar pool.

topic: hedging rules sit outside this policy
clause: These prohibitions are outlined in the Group's Hedging of Executive Awards and Performance Rights Policy.
why_it_matters: The operative hedging restrictions are in a separate document not lodged with this policy, so that policy must be reviewed before any collar is priced; it may be wider than the summary given here.

clause: Restricted Persons must not engage in short-term or speculative trading in Scentre Group Securities or in derivative or other Financial Products issued over or is respect of Scentre Group Securities. Short-term means in less than a 3-month period.
why_it_matters: The ban expressly reaches derivatives over the securities, so a collar must have a tenor of at least three months and should not contain early unwind or knock-out features that would make it short-term in substance.

clause: clearance to trade will not be given where the request to trade is based on considerations of a short-term or speculative nature
why_it_matters: The clearance application should present the collar as long-term risk management of a concentrated holding rather than a view on the price, since the Clearance Officer must refuse anything framed as short-term or speculative.

topic: OTC products may fall outside the Securities definition
clause: Scentre Group Securities means ... any Financial Products issued over or in respect of the above securities which are able to be traded on a financial market.
why_it_matters: A bilateral OTC collar may not be 'able to be traded on a financial market' and so may sit outside the clearance and blackout machinery on the literal wording, but section 11(d) regulates derivatives over the securities without that limit, so clearance should be sought regardless rather than relying on the gap.

clause: a clearance to trade can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or if there is a change in circumstances ... must complete the trade within three business days of the clearance being received, and fresh approval must be sought for any trades after this clearance period.
why_it_matters: The collar must be priced and executed within three business days of clearance, and clearance can be pulled before execution, so the bank's mandate should contemplate silent withdrawal and re-approval for any roll or restructure.

clause: if the clearance to trade is refused, the person seeking clearance must keep that information confidential.
why_it_matters: The executive cannot tell the bank why the trade cannot proceed, so documentation should not require a reason to be given for withdrawal.

topic: brokers with discretion must be notified
clause: Restricted Persons must also inform their brokers or financial advisers who have discretion to trade on their behalf that the Restricted Person is restricted from trading Scentre Group Securities under this policy.
why_it_matters: If any part of the structure gives the bank discretionary dealing authority over the securities, the bank must be formally notified of the trading restrictions.

clause: any other entity (including family companies, family trusts and personal superannuation funds) over which the Restricted Person or Restricted Person's immediate family member has, or may be expected to have, investment control or influence (including in its capacity as trustee or shareholder or unitholder)
why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan in a family trust, SMSF or personal company does not avoid clearance, the blackout periods or the section 11 prohibitions.

clause: the Chief Executive Officer has discretion to impose ad hoc restrictions on certain employees at times when matters subject to ASX Listing Rule 3.1A are being considered
why_it_matters: Entry, roll or unwind can be blocked at any time outside the scheduled blackout calendar and without public notice, so execution timing cannot be guaranteed to the counterparty.

clause: A blackout period is: (a) in respect of stapled securities of Scentre Group: the period commencing on 1 July ... and the period commencing on 1 January ...; and (b) in respect of units in the Carindale Property Trust: ...
why_it_matters: Scentre Group stapled securities are effectively closed from 1 January and 1 July until two hours after the relevant results release, leaving only narrow open windows in which a collar can be entered, amended or unwound.

clause: The Policy contains no prohibition on hedging, margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance, short selling or short-term dealing; the only reference to financing is the post-dealing disclosure of 'any margin lending or other security arrangement affecting those securities'.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares is not banned, so the structure turns entirely on window timing, Company Secretary clearance and disclosure rather than on any substantive prohibition.

clause: PME Securities include any derivatives of PME shares and securities (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise.
why_it_matters: Both collar legs, cash-settled or physically settled, are PME Securities, so each of entry, roll, unwind and settlement is a separate Dealing needing its own clearance and window.

clause: Dealing is generally confined to three 30-day Trading Windows: after the full-year results, after the half-year results and after the AGM.
why_it_matters: There are only about 90 dealing days a year, and the Chairman can shorten any window, so collar execution and any unwind must be scheduled tightly against the results and AGM calendar.

clause: Any Dealing must occur within 7 days of being so advised (and within 7 days of approval where the Chairman has approved an out-of-window Dealing).
why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of the collar and the secured loan must all complete inside a 7-day clearance life or the clearance must be re-obtained.

clause: the Dealing ... must comply with any conditions (including disclosure) which may be imposed by the Chairman (or in the case of the Chairman, the Board). Any approval given or conditions imposed are within the discretion of the Chairman.
why_it_matters: The Chairman can attach open-ended conditions, including public disclosure of the collar, as the price of any out-of-window execution.

topic: ad hoc blackouts and window truncation
clause: The Chairman can, as he or she deems appropriate, reduce the period of any Trading Window from time to time ... the Board or Chairman may, from time to time, declare any other period to be a 'Blackout Period'.
why_it_matters: A collar unwind, roll or physical settlement can be blocked at short notice by a declared Blackout Period or a truncated window, so the documentation needs cash settlement or deferral mechanics.

clause: Employees who acquire PME Securities under the Pro Medicus Share Plan, Pro Medicus Option Plan or any other employee incentive scheme from time to time must also comply with the rules of that Plan when Dealing in those securities.
why_it_matters: Hedging and encumbrance bans over unvested or plan-held shares may sit in the plan rules, which are not in this policy and must be diligenced separately before collaring plan shares.

clause: This Policy applies to all PME Directors and PME Employees. There is no definition of associates, and no extension to spouses, dependants, controlled entities or trusts.
why_it_matters: On its face the policy does not reach a family trust or controlled company holding the shares, though the Corporations Act insider trading prohibition and directors' notifiable interest obligations still bite.

clause: Strict compliance with this policy is a condition of employment. Breaches of this policy will be subject to disciplinary action, which may include termination of employment.
why_it_matters: A lender enforcement sale in a Blackout Period would be an unapproved Dealing by the borrower with dismissal risk, even though the policy is silent on forced sales.

clause: Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties must not use IAG Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including by: a. entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of IAG Securities; or b. transferring IAG Securities into an existing margin loan account.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is squarely prohibited for every Specified Person and their Closely Related Parties, with no approval or exceptional-circumstances route, so the structure cannot be offered to this population as designed.

clause: The prohibition is on collateral in 'any financial transaction'; the margin lending and margin account limbs are introduced by 'including by', so they are examples rather than the limit.
why_it_matters: Recharacterising the facility as a securities-backed loan, a limited recourse loan or a pledged prepaid forward does not escape clause 34.

clause: Securities means ... financial products (such as warrants, options, performance rights, contracts for difference and other derivatives) relating to, or which operate to limit, leverage or increase the economic risk in holding, those securities ... whether or not the securities or the financial products are issued or created by IAG Group or third parties.
why_it_matters: Both collar legs written by a bank are themselves IAG Securities, so entry, roll, exercise, unwind and settlement are each separate Dealings requiring their own consent within a Trading Window.

clause: IAG Securities acquired under an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by IAG by any participant must never be hedged prior to vesting ... IAG securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee, executive or director equity plan.
why_it_matters: Even an unfunded collar can only be placed over plan shares that have vested and are free of any holding lock, and the ban reaches Closely Related Parties so a family trust holding cannot be used.

clause: Dealings involving conditional orders must be placed and executed during a Trading Window (e.g., a specified, minimum sell or maximum purchase price or a stop-loss instruction).
why_it_matters: Any price-triggered feature of a collar - a knock-in or knock-out barrier, automatic unwind or stop-loss - must both trigger and complete inside a Trading Window, which is impractical for a multi-year structure.

clause: Where consent is required for a trade under this Policy, consent will not be granted where the approver does not consider that the trade would satisfy the front page test. This decision of the approver is final.
why_it_matters: A collar over an executive's shareholding is precisely the kind of trade that may be judged to look inappropriate on the front page, and the approver's refusal is final, unreasoned and confidential.

clause: Consent may be withdrawn if new information is revealed or there is a change in circumstances, and that decision to refuse consent is final and binding on the Specified Person seeking consent and must be kept confidential.
why_it_matters: A bank cannot rely on consent surviving to signing or settlement, and the executive cannot explain a withdrawal to the counterparty because it must be kept confidential.

clause: Consents to trade ... will be effective for 5 business days (but no later than the last day of the Trading Window), unless a different timeframe is specified in the consent provided.
why_it_matters: Pricing and execution of the derivative legs must complete within 5 business days and before the window closes, so documentation must be fully negotiated before consent is sought.

clause: Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties must not deal in IAG Securities on a short-term trading basis, being a period of three months between purchase and sale of any IAG Securities.
why_it_matters: Because derivatives are Securities with no stated carve-outs, a collar's purchased put and written call and any unwind must be spaced more than three months from related purchases and sales.

clause: Specified Persons must not assume that a Trading Window is open in the absence of notification, as the IAG Board may vary, suspend or terminate (conditionally or unconditionally) Trading Windows arrangements at any time.
why_it_matters: Execution and unwind dates cannot be committed in advance, since the Board can close a window at any time and the only relief is a discretionary Exceptional Circumstances consent.

clause: Clause 14's table routes consent requests from Non-Executive Directors of a Specified Board (excluding the IAG Board Chair) to the 'GCEO and Group General Counsel & Company Secretary', while the clause 36 roles table gives the IAG Board Chair responsibility to approve trading by other Non-Executive Directors, the GCEO and the Group General Counsel & Company Secretary.
why_it_matters: For a director-level collar the correct approver is ambiguous on the face of the Policy, so the bank should require evidence of consent from both the Chair and the Group General Counsel & Company Secretary.

clause: The Policy is silent on forced sales, margin calls, lender enforcement and pre-existing financing arrangements; there is no grandfathering wording accompanying the clause 34 prohibition added in the 30 November 2023 amendment.
why_it_matters: There is no carve-out permitting a secured lender to sell during a closed period, and no stated transition for legacy secured facilities, so any existing arrangement is exposed.

clause: Mandatory Holdings means the minimum holding of IAG ordinary shares required to be attained by IAG Directors and by the GCEO and GLT, in accordance with IAG's Mandatory Shareholding Requirement Policy.
why_it_matters: The separate Mandatory Shareholding Requirement Policy may require an unhedged minimum holding and must be diligenced, as this Policy neither operationalises nor excludes hedged shares.

clause: IAG Directors who undertake a Dealing in IAG Securities following consent must provide the Group Company Secretary within 1 business day of the execution of the trade a confirmation of trade so that an ASX Appendix 3Y can be completed and lodged with the ASX within 5 business days.
why_it_matters: A director's collar would become publicly disclosed on an Appendix 3Y within days of execution, which feeds back into the front page test at the consent stage.

clause: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities at any time, including in the exceptional circumstances referred to in section 6, unless the Restricted Person first obtains prior written clearance from [the Approving Officer].
why_it_matters: Clearance is required for every leg of a funded collar at any time of year, not just in Blackout Periods, so entry, roll, unwind and physical settlement each need a fresh written approval.

topic: secured lending is permitted with clearance
clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.
why_it_matters: Unlike policies with a flat ban, the loan leg secured on the collared shares is permissible here provided the Approving Officer gives prior written clearance, which makes a funded collar structurally available.

clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.
why_it_matters: The put and call legs over vested shares are a clearance decision rather than a prohibition, so the whole structure turns on the Chair's or Managing Director's willingness to approve.

clause: Restricted Persons are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.
why_it_matters: Absolute with no clearance route, so the collar and any security must be confined to shares that have already vested and been delivered.

clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is excluded from the section 5 restrictions].
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale over the collared shares in a Blackout Period does not put the executive in breach, which removes the single biggest obstacle most ASX policies present to a funded collar.

clause: Any written clearance granted under this policy will be valid for the period of five business days from the time which it is given or such other period as may be determined by the Approving Officer. The expiry time of the clearance will be stated in the clearance granted.
why_it_matters: The collar must be priced, documented and executed inside five business days unless the Approving Officer expressly extends the window in the clearance itself.

clause: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities within any period imposed by the Board from time to time ... Restricted Persons must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Period is in effect.
why_it_matters: An undisclosed Board-imposed Additional Period can block execution or unwind of the collar at any time, and the executive cannot even tell the bank why.

clause: the end of each of the March and September financial quarters and 24 hours immediately following the release of the Company's quarterly reports for those financial quarters
why_it_matters: As a mining company PLS has four closed periods a year rather than two, materially narrowing the windows in which a collar can be struck or unwound.

clause: Restricted Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading of Company Securities.
why_it_matters: Undefined, so a short-dated or knock-out collar risks being characterised as speculative; a multi-year tenor with no early termination triggers is safer.

clause: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise, (Company Securities)
why_it_matters: Both collar legs are themselves Company Securities, so acquiring the put and writing the call are separately 'trading' events needing clearance and falling outside Prohibited Periods.

clause: Where this policy requires a Restricted Person to do an act or thing, the relevant Restricted Person must do that act or thing in respect of the Connected Person.
why_it_matters: Booking the collar or loan through a family trust, controlled company or spouse does not avoid the clearance requirement; the executive must procure compliance.

clause: Breach of this policy (irrespective of whether the insider trading prohibition or any other law is breached) will also be regarded by the Group as serious misconduct which may lead to disciplinary action and/or dismissal.
why_it_matters: Executing any collar leg without written clearance is a dismissal-level offence, so the bank should condition drawdown on sighting the clearance.

company: WASHINGTON H. SOUL PATTINSON AND COMPANY LIMITED
clause: Directors, KMPs and Employees are prohibited from using margin loans to finance the purchase of securities in the Company or from trading in any financial products issued or created over the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: This is the decisive clause: both collar legs are financial products created over Company securities, so the derivative overlay is banned outright with no approval route, regardless of vesting state.

company: WASHINGTON H. SOUL PATTINSON AND COMPANY LIMITED
topic: hedging ban is narrower than the products ban
clause: must not trade in securities of the Company ... as part of a hedging arrangement if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting their exposure to Company securities that have not vested or are subject to a holding lock.
why_it_matters: Section 10 alone would permit hedging fully vested unrestricted shares, so any argument for a collar must overcome section 11.1 rather than section 10.1.

company: WASHINGTON H. SOUL PATTINSON AND COMPANY LIMITED
clause: prohibited from using margin loans to finance the purchase of securities in the Company
why_it_matters: The financing ban bites only on borrowing to buy Company shares, so a bank loan secured on an existing vested holding is not expressly prohibited, leaving the derivative legs as the sole blocker.

company: WASHINGTON H. SOUL PATTINSON AND COMPANY LIMITED
clause: The policy contains no provision on granting security, charges, liens or pledges over Company securities, on forced sales by a secured lender, on margin calls, or on disclosure of encumbrances.
why_it_matters: A lender enforcing security during a Closed Period has no express carve-out, so the executive would have to rely on the general 'no control or influence' exclusion in section 8.1 with no certainty.

company: WASHINGTON H. SOUL PATTINSON AND COMPANY LIMITED
clause: This is the case even if clearance to trade securities has been granted under this policy. Such clearance is taken to be revoked if the relevant person seeking to trade is in possession of non-public price sensitive information about or affecting the relevant securities.
why_it_matters: Approval is automatically void on receipt of inside information, so any structure must be executed immediately after approval and cannot rely on a standing consent.

company: WASHINGTON H. SOUL PATTINSON AND COMPANY LIMITED
clause: The written approval shall have effect for a period of four weeks from the date of the approval notice or a shorter period if specified in the notice unless a material change in circumstances occurs. ... Written approval to trade during a Prohibited Period is discretionary, is not an endorsement of the proposed trade and can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.
why_it_matters: Even the generous four-week exceptional-circumstances approval is expressly revocable, so a bank cannot treat it as a committed condition precedent.

company: WASHINGTON H. SOUL PATTINSON AND COMPANY LIMITED
clause: A decision to refuse approval to trade during a Prohibited Period is final and binding and must be kept confidential.
why_it_matters: There is no appeal and the executive cannot explain to the bank why a trade date was missed.

company: WASHINGTON H. SOUL PATTINSON AND COMPANY LIMITED
clause: This Policy applies to trading in the securities of Washington H. Soul Pattinson and Company Limited, those of its controlled and associated entities and those of entities in which it has a Substantial Interest [5% or more of the voting shares].
why_it_matters: A collar over shares in any listed investee in which SOL holds 5% or more also needs Chairman approval, which matters given SOL's investment portfolio.

company: WASHINGTON H. SOUL PATTINSON AND COMPANY LIMITED
clause: Sections 10.1 and 11.1 bind 'Directors, KMPs and Employees' whereas sections 2.2, 4.1, 5.1, 6.1 and 9.1 bind those persons 'and their Associates'.
why_it_matters: The drafting arguably leaves Associates outside the financial products ban, but the Associate definition and the approval requirement make any attempt to structure around it plainly against the policy's intent.

company: WASHINGTON H. SOUL PATTINSON AND COMPANY LIMITED
clause: A breach of this policy will be recorded, and serious breaches will be reported to the Leadership Team and the Board.
why_it_matters: Entering a collar without approval would be escalated to the Board rather than handled informally, with termination of employment expressly contemplated.

clause: The policy contains no clause prohibiting hedging. Instead, 'Other financial products that operate to limit the economic risk of holding SGH shares' are simply included in the definition of SGH securities.
why_it_matters: This is the key enabling feature: a collar is regulated as an ordinary dealing needing a window or clearance, rather than banned, and there is no ban on hedging unvested or restricted plan securities either.

topic: absolute blackout ban on derivative products
clause: In addition, during the blackout periods, no Executives or designated staff may deal in financial products issued or created over or in respect of SGH securities. No exceptional circumstances exemption applies to this prohibition.
why_it_matters: Collar entry, roll, unwind or any adjustment involving the option legs is absolutely impossible in a blackout period, with no hardship or court-order relief, so the bank must build hard date constraints into the trade.

clause: Any designated employee must obtain clearance in writing from the relevant approver detailed in the table in Section 3 for any proposed dealing in SGH securities in connection with a margin lending arrangement. ... Clearance may be granted subject to any conditions the approver determines appropriate.
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is permitted with clearance rather than prohibited, and the approver's power to impose conditions gives the company a way to protect itself rather than refuse outright.

clause: this policy does not apply to: ... A disposal of SGH securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a margin lending arrangement, where this policy has been complied with in relation to the margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: Lender enforcement over the collared shares, including in a blackout period, is outside the policy, but only if the underlying facility was itself properly cleared, so the bank should make clearance a condition precedent and retain evidence of it.

clause: Clearance may be given in any written form and is effective for two business days after it has been given.
why_it_matters: The collar and the loan must be documented in advance and executed within two business days of clearance, so pricing and legal work must be complete before the approval is sought.

clause: In the period between 24 hours and 30 working days after the release of SGH's Half Yearly Results announcement ... Annual Results announcements ... and the close of the SGHs Annual General Meeting.
why_it_matters: Three 30-working-day windows a year give ample scope to strike or unwind a collar without needing discretionary clearance at all.

clause: A designated employee must not be involved in a decision regarding their own application for clearance.
why_it_matters: For a Chairman or CEO collar the approval must come from the Lead Independent Director or ARC Chair, so the bank should verify who signed the clearance.

topic: no short-term or speculative trading rule
clause: The policy imposes no minimum holding period and no restriction on short-term or speculative dealing.
why_it_matters: Collar tenor is unconstrained by the policy, so short-dated or rolling structures are not objectionable on their face.

clause: Deal includes buying and selling, as well as procuring others to buy or sell.
why_it_matters: Granting security is not literally a Deal, so section 5 rather than the general definition is what brings the loan and any share transfer into the clearance net; a pledge unconnected to a lending arrangement sits in a gap.

clause: Associates of designated employees must comply with the policy as if they were a designated employee ... A breach of this policy, including a breach by an associate, will be regarded as serious misconduct.
why_it_matters: Booking the collar through a family trust or superannuation fund attracts the identical window, clearance and blackout constraints and the employee bears the consequences.

clause: All designated employees and their associates must obtain approval prior to trading in the securities of listed entities in which SGH has a Substantial Interest (including controlled and associated entities) [Appendix 1: Beach Energy (BPT), Boral (BLD), Seven West Media (SWM)].
why_it_matters: A collar over Beach Energy, Boral or Seven West Media shares held by an SGH designated employee also requires prior approval under this policy.

clause: The following transactions relating to trading in the Company's securities are excluded from the operation of this policy: ... a disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising its rights.
why_it_matters: This is the single most collar-friendly clause in the policy: the bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares, including a sale in a closed period, falls outside the policy altogether, so the executive does not breach by reason of the lender enforcing.

clause: The policy contains no margin lending, secured financing, pledge or encumbrance prohibition of any kind, and no disclosure obligation in respect of any such facility.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is unrestricted, which is unusual among ASX policies and removes the usual blocking provision.

clause: Directors and employees are prohibited from trading during prohibited periods in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: The put and call legs are financial products over Lynas securities, so entry, amendment, roll, unwind and any cash or physical settlement of the collar must all be timed to fall inside a three-week open window.

clause: All periods other than the periods referred to in paragraphs 7.1 and 9.2 are “closed periods” during which all directors and employees are generally prohibited from Dealing in Securities of the Company.
why_it_matters: Lynas is closed by default and open only for three weeks after results, the AGM or a prospectus, so there may be as little as four short windows a year in which a collar can be struck or unwound.

clause: clearance may be given by the Chairman and at least one other non-executive director for the director or employee to sell (but not to purchase) securities when he or she otherwise would not be permitted to do so.
why_it_matters: Out-of-window relief is confined to selling, so it cannot be used to buy back a written call, close out a put or enter a collar outside a window; only an outright sale of the underlying can be cleared.

topic: hedging ban limited to unvested options
clause: Directors and employees must not at any time hedge options issued to them under an employee option plan prior to vesting of the options.
why_it_matters: The hedging prohibition is confined to unvested employee options, so a collar over vested shares is not caught by it, but unvested option entitlements must be excluded from the collared parcel.

clause: Directors and employees must not at any time engage in short-term trading in securities of the Company.
why_it_matters: With no defined holding period, a short-dated collar or one with early termination or roll features risks being characterised as short-term trading, so a long tenor and confirmation from the Chairman or Secretary at clearance are advisable.

clause: the Chairman or Secretary has indicated in writing that there is no impediment to them doing so; and the proposed Dealing is permitted under paragraph 7.1 or 9.2.
why_it_matters: The policy sets no window within which a cleared trade must be executed and no express revocation right, so the bank should document that the written no-impediment confirmation is current at pricing and at each subsequent leg.

clause: directors and employees should consider this policy to be binding on them in the absence of specific exemption by the board.
why_it_matters: The board can exempt a specific transaction from the policy entirely, which offers a route to sanction a collar whose timing or structure does not fit the narrow windows.

clause: This policy has been implemented to prevent the incidence of 'insider trading' ... by directors and employees and persons associated with any of them. ... a director or employee must not recommend or otherwise suggest to any person (including a spouse, relative, friend, trustee of a family trust or directors of a family company) that they buy or sell securities in the Company.
why_it_matters: Associates are referred to in the introduction but no associate is defined and no operative rule binds them, so a collar entered by a spouse or family trust sits in an untested area rather than a clearly permitted or prohibited one.

clause: Directors must notify the company secretary immediately on acquiring or disposing of a relevant interest in any securities in the Company.
why_it_matters: Entering the collar may change the director's relevant interest, or be treated as doing so on physical settlement, triggering immediate notice to the company secretary and an Appendix 3Y within 5 Business Days that will disclose the structure publicly.

clause: Directors and Designated Persons are not permitted at any time (including outside any Closed Period) to enter into any hedging instruments or arrangements regarding or derivative financial products issued over any APA Securities held by the Director or Designated Person.
why_it_matters: This single clause defeats the funded collar: both the purchased put and the written call are derivative financial products issued over APA Securities held by the executive, and the ban is absolute in time, indifferent to vesting, and has no clearance or exemption route.

clause: Directors and Designated Persons may include APA Securities in a diversified portfolio under a margin loan facility or secured financing arrangement provided that: the facility or arrangement does not permit title to the APA Securities to be transferred.
why_it_matters: Even setting the derivatives ban aside, the loan leg fails on its own terms: a facility secured solely on the collared APA parcel is not a diversified portfolio, and any title-transfer collateral or rehypothecation right is expressly prohibited, so only a non-title-transfer security interest inside a broader portfolio facility is permitted.

clause: Directors and Designated Persons may not at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any APA Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock, to secure any obligation of that person, or any third party.
why_it_matters: Unvested and holding-locked securities are unavailable as collateral in any structure, and the words 'directly or indirectly' and 'or any third party' block back-to-back or guarantee arrangements over that stock.

clause: to avoid doubt, the terms of this policy will continue to apply to the relevant APA Securities, including the requirement that they not be disposed of in a Closed Period unless permission for such disposal is granted pursuant to section 4.2.7.
why_it_matters: A margin call or enforcement sale during a Closed Period is not an excluded dealing and requires exceptional circumstances permission from the Chairman, so a lender cannot rely on unfettered enforcement rights and the borrower bears the timing risk.

clause: Clearance to undertake a proposed dealing will be valid for three business days or until a Closed Period commences, whichever is the shorter period.
why_it_matters: Any permitted dealing in the underlying must be priced and executed within three business days, and a clearance may be withdrawn if circumstances change, which constrains any multi-leg execution.

clause: The decision to give or refuse clearance is in the absolute discretion of the Recipient and is final and binding on the Applicant, and reasons for the decision need not be provided. ... If clearance is refused, the Applicant must keep the fact of that refusal confidential.
why_it_matters: There is no appeal and no obligation to explain, and the executive cannot tell a bank counterparty why a transaction cannot proceed, so financing documents should not require disclosure of the reason for a refusal.

clause: the guiding principle is that Directors and Designated Persons who purchase APA Securities should intend, at the time of acquisition, to continue to hold the purchased APA Securities for at least the next 12 months.
why_it_matters: Any structure with an economic tenor of under 12 months, or that contemplates repurchasing securities delivered under the collar, risks being treated as short-term or speculative trading.

topic: same open period buy and sell
clause: Directors and Designated Persons must not both buy and sell APA Securities in the same “open” period between two consecutive Closed Periods.
why_it_matters: Physical settlement of a collar combined with any purchase in the same open window would breach this rule, so delivery and any repurchase must straddle a Closed Period.

clause: APA Group requires that Directors and Designated Persons take all reasonable steps to cause their respective Related Parties to comply with this section 4.2 as if they were Directors or Designated Persons.
why_it_matters: Holding the collared stock through a spouse, resident child, family trust, superannuation fund or significantly influenced company does not escape the hedging ban or the financing conditions.

clause: derivative financial products issued over any APA Securities held by the Director or Designated Person.
why_it_matters: The ban is drafted by reference to securities held, so a cash-settled index or basket derivative not referable to a held parcel is arguably outside 4.2.5, though it would still face the short selling and short-term trading prohibitions in 4.2.4.

clause: other persons specified from time to time by the Managing Director ... The Company Secretary will operate a process for regularly reviewing the list of Designated Persons and maintain a register of Designated Persons, and will notify relevant individuals of their inclusion on or removal from the register.
why_it_matters: An executive outside section 4.2 today can be brought within it at the Managing Director's discretion, so any structure entered by a non-Designated employee should be documented to survive, or be unwound on, later designation.

clause: If it becomes apparent that a Director has breached this policy, APA Group will give careful consideration to whether it ought to make an announcement to the market explaining the circumstances of the breach and what, if any, remedial and/or disciplinary action it has taken.
why_it_matters: A breach by a Director carries express reputational exposure through a possible market announcement, raising the stakes on any structure that sits close to the 4.2.5 line.

clause: You must not engage in transactions in the derivative markets involving products based on Xero Securities. This includes OTC products ... caps and collars and any other financial product that operates to limit the economic risk associated with Xero Securities.
why_it_matters: This is one of the few ASX policies that names 'collars' and 'OTC products' expressly, so the derivative legs of a funded collar are prohibited on their face rather than merely caught by a definition.

topic: exceptional circumstances as the only derivatives gate
clause: You may apply for approval to enter into one of these transactions in exceptional circumstances. Approval will not be given in relation to unvested Xero Securities.
why_it_matters: A collar over vested shares is not absolutely barred, but it can only proceed through an exceptional-circumstances application (severe hardship, court order or similar), which a commercial monetisation is unlikely to satisfy.

clause: Whether or not you are a Designated Person, you must seek clearance ... before you: enter into a margin loan or other secured financing arrangements (including transferring Xero Securities into an existing margin loan account); grant a security or rights over your Xero Securities.
why_it_matters: The loan and security legs of a funded collar are permitted with clearance, so the structure fails only on the derivative legs; a plain secured loan against Xero shares without a hedge is available.

clause: You must not enter into an arrangement or transaction that ... otherwise enables you to profit from a decrease in the market price of Xero Securities.
why_it_matters: This limb is not restricted to unvested holdings and independently catches the purchased put in a collar over fully vested shares.

clause: Xero takes a 'substance over form' approach and has regard to the intent and spirit of this policy when applying and enforcing it.
why_it_matters: Structuring around the derivatives ban (for example a non-recourse loan with an economically equivalent payoff, or a hedge booked at a Connected Person entity) will be assessed on its economic substance.

clause: Where clearance is required to deal under this policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not meet the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Even the permitted secured financing leg can be refused on reputational grounds alone, without reasons being given.

clause: They may also decide to impose conditions on the dealing or withdraw the clearance at any time. If your clearance is not approved or is withdrawn, you must keep this fact confidential. Clearance is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if you become aware of Inside Information prior to dealing.
why_it_matters: A bank cannot rely on a granted clearance surviving to signing or drawdown; it can be withdrawn at any time or lapse automatically, and the executive cannot explain why.

clause: Your Connected Persons should only deal in Xero Securities in circumstances where you yourself would be permitted to do so. Where clearance requirements would apply to your dealing, you must comply with those requirements on behalf of your Connected Persons.
why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan in a family trust or controlled company does not avoid the derivatives ban or the clearance obligation.

clause: Short term dealing is the buying and selling of listed securities within a 6 month period.
why_it_matters: A collar with a tenor under six months, or one whose entry and physical settlement fall within six months, risks characterisation as short-term dealing on top of the derivatives ban.

topic: no venue limitation and no vesting limitation on the derivatives ban
clause: any other financial product that operates to limit the economic risk associated with Xero Securities
why_it_matters: Unlike venue-limited bans elsewhere, this catch-all covers OTC bank-written puts and calls over on-market as well as plan-sourced shares.
